visual: Low, vigorous evergreen carpeting perennial forming a dense mat of exceptionally soft, woolly silver-grey leaves. 'Silver Carpet' is grown mainly for foliage and flowers only sparsely compared with typical lamb's ear.
water: Water during establishment, then only during prolonged dry periods.
soil: Moderately fertile, well-drained chalk, loam or sandy soil; tolerant of acid, neutral or alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Protect from excessive winter wet. Poor drainage can cause foliage and crown deterioration.
prune: No routine pruning required. Remove damaged or untidy foliage as needed.
hardinessNote: Extremely hardy, below -20°C; RHS rates this cultivar H7.
resilience: Exceptionally cold hardy, drought tolerant once established and effective as dense weed-suppressing ground cover, but less tolerant of prolonged winter wet.
uses: Ground cover, gravel gardens, border edging, sensory planting, rose underplanting and sunny dry borders.
foliage: Evergreen; dense, soft, elliptic grey-white to silver leaves up to around 10 cm long.
container: Suitable for sunny containers with very free-draining compost.
uncertain: 'Silver Carpet' is notably less floriferous than typical Stachys byzantina and is primarily selected for its dense silver foliage.
